text: Track 4.1 The topic of today's seminar is how climate change is affecting the Earth's various climates. At the beginning of the 19th century, Vladimir Köppen, a German scientist, organised the world's climates into five categories, which we still use today. Global warming is affecting each of these climates in different ways. Let's begin with tropical climates, which are hot and humid, with lots of rain. A tropical climate has temperatures higher than 18 degrees Celsius all year. Countries near the equator have tropical climates, including Brazil and Colombia in South America, the Congo in Africa and Malaysia and Indonesia in Asia. As the weather gets hotter, they receive less rain. This affects the rainforests. There are more forest fires, which kill lots of wildlife. People are also cutting down the rainforests, so many types of animals, plants and trees could disappear forever. We need to look after the rainforests to save the plants and wildlife. And also, because rainforests help to slow down global warming for the whole planet. Next, the dry climate. A dry climate is one in which there isn't a lot of rain. There are two types of desert climates, hot and cold. Hot desert climates have hot temperatures all year round. For example, Australia, most countries in the Middle East and North Africa. On the other hand, cold desert climates have hot summers and cold winters, such as Argentina and Chile in South America, some countries in Central Asia. In the future, the weather in these places will become even hotter and drier. There will be droughts and people will need to use water very carefully. Some areas, like Central Australia, could become so hot that people just won't be able to live there anymore. At the other extreme is the polar climate, the areas covering the North and South Pole. The weather here is very cold, with temperatures never higher than 10 degrees Celsius. The warmer global temperatures mean that the ice here is melting and sea levels are rising. Scientists believe that Arctic and Antarctic wildlife are in danger due to the changing environment. The final two categories we are going to talk about are the temperate climate, which has warm, humid summers and mild winters. The continental climate has warm to cool summers and very cold winters.
